newsitem.title: CANADA: Investors focus on mining exploration stocks.
newsitem.headline: Investors focus on mining exploration stocks.

text.p: Junior mining stocks were popular on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday as investors placed their bets on the next big discovery, analysts said.
"There's quite a lot of money around the stock market, and people are willing to speculate on trying to find the next Bre-X," said mining analyst Michael Fowler at Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion.
Pure Gold Resources Inc topped the most-actives list on the Toronto Stock Exchange once again on Thursday, with almost 11 million shares trading hands before noon. The stock rose C$0.05 to C$0.45.
The stock has headed up steadily from C$0.20 on January 23 since announced drilling results from its diamond property in north-central Alberta earlier this week.
The first two holes of the drilling program intersected kimberlitic rocks, the company said.
Golden Rule Resources Ltd was active again on Thursday morning, rising C$0.15 to C$10.20 with more than one million shares trading hands by noon.
Golden Rule caught the market's attention when it announced trenching results from its gold exploration property in Ghana earlier this month.

The stock peaked at C$13.10 earlier this week, rising from C$5.20 on January 6, but the price began to slide on Tuesday after analysts warned that exploration was still young and the shares had climbed too high too fast.
Golden Rule also announced on Tuesday it was reassessing operations at its Komis gold mine in Saskatchewan because of lower gold prices.

Investors also had their eyes on Rex Diamond Mining Corp after the company said this week that an independent consultant valued the company's Tongo Fields properties in Sierra Leone at US$3.3 billion, with resources totalling 18.9 million carats.
More than 855,000 Rex Diamond shares had traded hands by midday on Thursday, pushing the stock up C$0.40 to C$3.75.
